ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A cylindrical barrel with radius $4$ feet and height $10$ feet is full of water. A solid cube with side length $8$ feet is set into the barrel so that the diagonal of the cube is vertical. The volume of water thus displaced is $v$ cubic feet. Find $v^2$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an open cylindrical bucket, with the bucket opening drawn as an ellipse; a cube is placed obliquely into the bucket opening, and dashed lines above and inside indicate hidden edges or diagonals. The cube has one lower vertex entering the bucket, and the plane of the bucket opening intersects the three edges adjacent to this lower vertex, so the submerged part corresponds to a tetrahedron at one corner. Reasoning: The cylinder radius is 4 ft and the height is 10 ft; the cube side length is 8 ft. Take the lower submerged cube vertex as the origin, and the three adjacent edges as the positive x,y,z axes. Since one space diagonal of the cube is vertical, the vertical axis is x=y=z. The horizontal plane of the bucket opening can be written as x+y+z=c, and its intersections with the three edges are (c,0,0), (0,c,0), (0,0,c). The distance from these points to the vertical axis x=y=z is c√(2/3). The bucket radius is 4, so c√(2/3)=4, giving c=2√6. Since c<8, the intersection points are indeed on the three edges of the cube; the submerged depth is c/√3=2√2<10, also less than the bucket height. The volume of displaced water is exactly the volume of this corner tetrahedron, v=c^3/6=(2√6)^3/6=8√6. Therefore v^2=(8√6)^2=384.

method.method_draft: First read the image as showing a cube tilted so that one body diagonal is vertical, with its lower corner entering the circular top of the full cylindrical barrel; the barrel rim/water surface cuts the three cube edges adjacent to that lower corner, so the submerged part is a corner tetrahedron. From the text, take barrel radius 4 ft, cube side 8 ft, and barrel height 10 ft. Set coordinates at the submerged cube corner, with the three cube edges as the positive coordinate axes; the vertical body diagonal is the line x=y=z, so a horizontal rim plane has equation x+y+z=c. The three rim intersection points are (c,0,0), (0,c,0), (0,0,c). Their distance from the vertical axis x=y=z is c√(2/3), and the barrel rim radius makes this equal to 4. Solve c=2√6, check c<8 and depth c/√3<10, then compute the displaced volume as the simplex volume c^3/6. Square the resulting v.

图像描述：图中是一个开口圆柱桶，桶口画成椭圆；一个立方体倾斜放入桶口，上方和内部用虚线表示被遮挡的棱或对角线。立方体有一个较低的顶点进入桶内，桶口平面与这个较低顶点相邻的三条棱相交，因此入水部分对应一个角上的四面体。

method.method_draft: First read the image as a geometric setup where the circular barrel rim is the water surface and it intersects the cube around the lower vertex, forming an equilateral triangular cross-section whose three vertices lie on the circular rim. From the text, use radius R=4 and cube side 8. Let t be the distance from the lower cube corner along each of the three mutually perpendicular cube edges to the waterline. The submerged portion is a tri-rectangular tetrahedron with three perpendicular edges of length t, volume v=t^3/6; then square v.

再推理：桶半径为 R=4，立方体边长为 8。设从立方体较低顶点沿三条互相垂直的棱到水面的距离都为 t。由于立方体的空间对角线竖直，这三个交点关于竖直轴对称，所以它们形成等边三角形截面。该三角形每条边连接两条互相垂直棱上的点，因此边长为 t√2。这个等边三角形内接于桶口圆，圆的半径就是其外接圆半径 4。等边三角形外接圆半径满足 R=s/√3，所以 4=(t√2)/√3。解得 t=4√3/√2=2√6。浸入水中的部分是一个三棱直角四面体，其三条互相垂直的棱长均为 t，所以体积 v=t^3/6=(2√6)^3/6=8√6。因此 v^2=(8√6)^2=64·6=384。
